item.title: Tech stock selloff after AI leaders call for slowdown in development
item.description: Calls for a slowdown in AI development sparked a global selloff in tech stocks on Monday. Jessica Inskip, the director of investor research at StockBrokers.com, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Who won Emmys for 2026? See the full winners list here.
item.description: The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards celebrated the best in television and streaming from the past year on Monday. See the full list of winners and nominees.

item.title: Oil prices stay above $100 as Iran and Oman delay Strait of Hormuz talks
item.description: Iran and Oman delayed a meeting to discuss control of the Strait of Hormuz as fighting between Iran's Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia raises the stakes for global energy markets.

item.title: Supreme Court blocks new Postal Service rules for mail ballots in blow to Trump
item.description: The Supreme Court left intact a ruling that blocked the U.S. Postal Service from enforcing new regulations for mail voting, rejecting the Trump administration's effort to move forward with the rules in the midterms.

item.title: Trump nominates Lee Greenwood's wife to serve as ambassador to Barbados
item.description: President Trump on Monday nominated Kimberly Greenwood, the wife of "God Bless the USA" singer Lee Greenwood, to serve as ambassador to Barbados and several other Caribbean countries.

item.title: Blanche defends mail ballot changes, says election practices are being probed
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche fiercely defended the Trump administration's push to impose tighter mail voting rules, telling CBS News the DOJ is examining election practices in multiple states.

item.title: Vance says 870K people suspected of COVID-era U.S. fraud barred from federal loans
item.description: A U.S. enforcement push, dubbed "Heartland fraud surge," probed losses involving the Paycheck Protection Program and Economic Injury Disaster Loan program.

item.title: Rep. Sam Liccardo urges lawmakers "to take action" on AI: "Instead, in Congress, we see vacation"
item.description: While artificial intelligence leaders are uniting to slow development, lawmakers are split over the government's role in regulating the industry and how to balance safety concerns with efforts to stay ahead of China in the AI race. Democratic Rep. Sam Liccardo of California joins CBS News with his take.

item.title: Arkansas head coach John Calipari explains why he's backing the Protect College Sports Act
item.description: President Trump is urging Congress to pass the Protect College Sports Act. It would establish new guidelines and protections for name, image and likeness payments, and regulate issues like the transfer portal and how much teams can spend on their rosters. University of Arkansas head coach John Calipari joins to discuss his support for the bill.

item.title: Vance says those suspected of defrauding COVID-era programs barred from future federal loans
item.description: Vice President JD Vance announced on Monday that people suspected of defrauding COVID-era programs will be barred from future federal loans.

item.title: EPA to eliminate limits on climate pollution from power plants
item.description: The rule, which is expected to face immediate legal challenges, also could prevent future administrations from regulating greenhouse gas emissions from power plants, sources said.

item.title: Democrats vow to investigate Trump pardon brokers if party controls Congress
item.description: Senior Democratic lawmakers vowed to investigate the new market that has sprung up around President Trump's pardons, citing CBS News video that aired in a 60 Minutes report.

item.title: Jeffries calls for immediate congressional action on artificial intelligence
item.description: On Capitol Hill, lawmakers returning from the summer recess are weighing in with differing views on how much government regulation on artificial intelligence is necessary. New York Times congressional correspondent Robert Jimison joins to discuss.

item.title: EPA moves to eliminate rule limiting greenhouse gas emissions from power plants
item.description: The Environmental Protection Agency is moving to axe a restriction that limits greenhouse gas emissions from power plants. Bloomberg News reporter Zahra Hirji joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Extended interview: Trump AI adviser David Sacks on tech leaders' AI fears
item.description: David Sacks, a key adviser to President Trump on technology, believes fears that AI could threaten humanity are overblown. In an exclusive interview with CBS News' Jo Ling Kent, Sacks delivers a message to tech leaders including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, argues that a "pause" on AI development could cause the U.S. to fall behind China in the AI race, and discusses more about the importance of tech.

item.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump mail ballot restrictions for now
item.description: The Supreme Court on Monday blocked the Postal Service's new rules for mail ballots while a legal challenge plays out, in a blow to President Trump's agenda. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks down the ruling.

item.title: What could a global pause on AI look like?
item.description: Several top tech CEOs are calling for a slowdown in artificial intelligence development amid industry concerns that the technology is spiraling out of control. In a recent New York Times opinion piece, investigative journalist Stephen Witt argues that slowing down may not be enough. Witt joins CBS News to explain.

item.title: 70-year-old hiker found after he was missing for a week
item.description: A 70-year-old hiker, lost for a week on a large island in the middle of Lake Superior, has been found, after search and rescue teams had nearly given up hope. Mark Strassmann has the story.

item.title: Don Jr.'s wife says Russian oligarch hosted post-wedding festivities as a "gift"
item.description: Bettina Anderson, wife of Donald Trump Jr., said their "dear friend" Umar Kremlev hosted two nights of festivities after their wedding in the Bahamas.

item.title: Looking back at Bob Mackie's signature looks, life after his death at 87
item.description: Bob Mackie, a fashion icon known for elevating Hollywood's leading ladies and pop stars for decades, died on Monday at 87. Meg Oliver looks back on his signature looks and his life.

item.title: Alligator Alcatraz had cramped conditions, "small metal enclosures," watchdog finds
item.description: DHS's internal watchdog is sharply criticizing conditions in a Florida immigration detention center dubbed "Alligator Alcatraz," finding detainees at the now-closed facility were held in "cramped conditions."

item.title: Tech stocks slump after AI execs call for industry slowdown
item.description: The tech-heavy Nasdaq slumped 147 points on Monday after AI company executives called for a slowdown in developing the technology.

item.title: AI companies must ensure their tech is safe, says top Trump adviser on AI
item.description: In an interview with CBS News, Sacks suggested that fears AI could harm people are overblown. "I think this is becoming a panic," he said.

item.title: Trump says U.S. needs a "high IQ" president to handle AI
item.description: Over the weekend, Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei published a 3,800-word essay calling for a global slowdown in the exponential development of artificial intelligence. Sam Altman, who runs OpenAI, Elon Musk and others shared social media posts agreeing with Amodei's assessment. CBS News Washington correspondent Natalie Brand has President Trump's reaction.

item.title: 9/14: CBS Evening News
item.description: AI executives and President Trump disagree over doomsday warnings; the president blames Ukraine for high oil and gas prices.

item.title: Mitch McConnell returns to Capitol Hill after monthslong absence
item.description: GOP Sen. Mitch McConnell of Kentucky returned to Capitol Hill on Monday for the first time in three months, ending a prolonged absence that sparked widespread speculation about his health.

item.title: The AI bubble is leaking air, some economists say. Should investors worry?
item.description: AI has fueled a stock boom in recent years. Now, some Wall Street analysts think that epic run is coming to an end.

item.title: As AI rhetoric heats up, Congress stalls on action
item.description: Some House Democrats are calling on Speaker Mike Johnson to delay the congressional recess expected at the end of the week until lawmakers pass AI safeguards.

item.title: Pardon brokers offer to "put pressure on the president," at sky-high costs
item.description: Hidden cameras captured lobbyists as they tried to woo a potential client interested in obtaining a pardon from President Trump.

item.title: New testosterone guidelines temporarily rescinded, Pentagon says
item.description: The Pentagon will begin requiring male service members ages 30 and older to get screened for testosterone deficiency, after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called for the change over the summer.
